t: You're standing where Bath House once was, a London town house that has since been demolished. In the nineteenth century it belonged to the Barons Ashburton. The site had held the Pulteney Hotel, and in 1821 Alexander Baring bought the property from William Pulteney, the Earl of Bath. Baring rebuilt it and named it after the Earl. Baring was a politician, diplomat and financier, later the first Baron Ashburton. Pulteney sat in the House of Commons for over three decades before becoming Earl of Bath in 1742.
